title: Financial Literacy and Financial Health of Public Junior High School Teachers
tldr: Filipino public school teachers demonstrate high financial literacy but are 'financially coping,' with notable gaps in retirement planning and emergency fund building, highlighting the need for targeted financial wellness training.
problem_and_motivation: Despite the critical role of public school teachers, there is a scarcity of localized research examining their financial literacy and financial health. Low wages, rising living costs, and limited financial planning support create financial insecurity among Filipino educators, which may affect their professional effectiveness and quality of life.
approach: Quantitative-descriptive research using validated questionnaires (adapted from Financial Health Network 2024 and Surendar & Subramanya Sarma 2018) with 241 public junior high school teachers from District VI, Quezon City. Used Kruskal-Wallis H and Mann-Whitney U tests for group comparisons. Financial literacy assessed across: financial knowledge, behavior, attitude, budgeting/tax, liquidity management, investment, and retirement planning. Financial health assessed across: spending, saving, borrowing, and planning.
findings: Teachers demonstrated high overall financial literacy (mean 4.02) but were classified as 'financially coping' (financial health mean 61.2). Notable gaps emerged in retirement planning (3.75), emergency fund preparedness, and balancing savings with borrowing. Significant demographic differences in financial literacy were found by sex, age, income, education, position, experience, and specialization. Financial health showed significant differences by sex, age, civil status, number of children, education, position, experience, and specialization.

definitions.Financial Literacy: The ability to make informed decisions regarding budgeting, saving, investing, and planning
definitions.Financially Coping: A classification indicating individuals can manage daily financial demands but face challenges in building long-term financial security
definitions.Financially Vulnerable: A classification indicating limited financial reserves and susceptibility to financial shocks

limitations: Cross-sectional design limits ability to establish causation
Self-reported data may introduce response bias
Focus on a single district in Quezon City limits generalizability
Only public junior high school teachers studied; excludes other educator levels
Does not account for broader socioeconomic factors beyond demographics
remember_this: Filipino public school teachers have high financial literacy knowledge but are 'financially coping' — managing daily expenses but struggling with long-term security. Targeted financial wellness training is needed, especially in retirement planning, emergency fund building, and debt management strategies.
